Conformance · Source: mqlite main · docs/conformance.md — source v0.4.2 with unreleased changes. Latest supported release: v0.4.2. These docs track main; use the linked release for published artifacts.

Conformance — correct mqlite behavior (TCK)

This specification follows main, including unreleased changes. For an installed v0.4.2 release, use the conformance specification at that tag; see CHANGELOG.md for pending behavior changes.

This is the normative spec of how mqlite must behave — the invariants that define "correct," independent of any one implementation detail. Each is enforced by a hermetic test (cross-referenced); together these are mqlite's TCK. If a change would break a MUST here, it is a behavior change, not a refactor.

Default Peek-Lock delivery is at-least-once: redelivery is possible, so handlers must be idempotent. Receive-and-delete is the caller's explicit at-most-once broker-removal path and removes a message before returning it; the same receive attempt ID can replay its saved response. Other documented discard paths include message TTL configured to discard, DLQ retention, forced resource deletion, and fixed subscription expiry. (§1.7, §3, §8, §14)

1 · Peek-Lock lifecycle

  • 1.1 Receive claims an active message, moving it to locked for the queue's lock duration, and returns a lock_token. (engine/functional_test.go)

  • 1.2 A locked message MUST be invisible to other Receive calls until it is settled, its lock expires, or explicit embedded startup recovery invalidates the orphaned lock. Ordinary startup MUST preserve an unexpired lease on an active resource because another holder may survive that open; resource lifecycle and message TTL still apply. Within one running broker, no live lease is granted twice. (engine/functional_test.go TestCompetingConsumersNoDouble)

  • 1.3 Each newly granted Receive or ReceiveDeferred claim increments delivery_count exactly once. Renewal, settlement, lock reaping, scheduled activation and replay of a live receive attempt MUST NOT increment it. (engine/engine_test.go, engine/ga_fixes_test.go, engine/functional_test.go)

  • 1.4 When a lock expires, the reaper returns the message to active (redelivery) — or to dead_lettered once delivery_count >= max_delivery_count. (engine/engine_test.go)

  • 1.5 Claims are O(log n) on a deep backlog (a partial index on active rows; the reaper, not the claim path, reclaims expired locks). (engine/claim_plan_test.go)

  • 1.6 Claim time. Receive (with or without an AttemptID, including receive-and-delete) and ReceiveDeferred MUST evaluate TTL eligibility and lease deadlines using fresh broker time after writer admission, for each claimed item and each remote retry. A message whose TTL has expired at that check MUST NOT be claimed. Waiting for the writer or processing an earlier batch item MUST NOT consume a later item's lease before its claim begins. (engine/functional_test.go: TestClaimTimeAfterWriterAdmission, TestClaimBatchUsesEachItemsTime, TestClaimBatchTTLBetweenItems, TestReceiveDeferredMixedItemsAndCommittedPrefix; engine/storage_test.go: TestClaimTimeRefreshesOnRemoteRetry)

  • 1.7 Receive-and-delete removes each returned row and grants no lease: its lock token is empty and deadline is zero, including a cached attempt replay. Peek-lock retains its token and lease deadline. (sdk_test.go: TestSDKReceiveDeleteLeaseShape)

  • 1.8 Queue lock configuration. A new or explicitly reconfigured queue MUST use 0 (the 30-second default) or a lock duration from 1 second through 1 hour, inclusive. Values outside that range fail with ErrInvalidArgument before any mutation. Existing databases with a legacy value outside the range remain readable; an update that does not overwrite the backing queue configuration may preserve that value. (engine/engine_test.go: TestQueueLockDurationValidation, TestLegacyOutOfRangeQueuesRemainReadable; sdk_test.go: TestQueueLockDurationValidationBeforeTransport)

2 · Settlement (fenced on lock_token)

Exactly one verb per outcome; new effects require the lock_token from Receive and an unexpired lease, with the exact-request replay exception in §2.6.

  • 2.1 Complete removes the message. (engine/functional_test.go)
  • 2.2 Abandon returns it to active for redelivery (or dead_lettered at/above max). With delay_ms > 0 it parks in scheduled until the backoff lapses (scheduler re-activates it); on an ordered queue the parked head holds head-of-line exactly like a scheduled send — successors cannot overtake it (§5.5). Neither Abandon nor scheduled activation increments delivery_count; the next claim does. (engine/engine_test.go; engine/functional_test.go: TestAbandonDelayHoldsGroupOrder)
  • 2.3 Reject moves it to dead_lettered with a reason. (engine/functional_test.go)
  • 2.4 Defer sets it aside; it is retrieved later by seq via ReceiveDeferred. Normal Receive never returns a deferred message. In an ordered queue a deferred message holds the head-of-line — later messages in its group (or the whole queue under strict_fifo) are not claimable until it is retrieved and settled; other groups proceed. There is no automatic recovery without a TTL (the reaper never reclaims deferred rows); recover a lost seq via Peek state=deferred. A successful ReceiveDeferred increments delivery_count but does not gate that explicit by-sequence claim on max_delivery_count; it can therefore return a count above the ordinary delivery budget. Subsequent settlement follows the usual rules. (engine/functional_test.go: TestDeferHoldsHeadOfLine)
  • 2.5 Renew MUST preserve the same state, token, and delivery_count. For a queue or subscription without a fixed expiry it sets the deadline to max(old locked_until, broker now + lock_duration); a fixed subscription lifetime caps the candidate deadline. It MUST NOT shorten a lease or revive one whose current deadline has passed. (engine/ga_fixes_test.go)
  • 2.6 Settling with a wrong/expired token MUST fail with ErrLockLost (HTTP 409) — except an idempotent replay with a live receipt for the exact request (§3.2) returns success. Matching the token alone is insufficient: new settlement and renewal effects require a locked row with locked_until_ms > now, including before the reaper runs. The equality boundary is expired. Time is sampled after local writer admission and afresh for each settlement statement and remote retry; waiting cannot preserve an expired lease or receipt. A live exact-request receipt can still replay a previously committed effect after the original lease expires. (engine/ga_fixes_test.go; engine/complete_batch_test.go: TestSettlementLeaseDeadline, TestSettlementReceiptIdentityMatrix, TestSettlementReceiptTimeAfterWriterAdmission, TestCompleteBatchRefreshesTimeBetweenChunks; engine/storage_test.go: TestSettlementTimeRefreshesOnRemoteRetry; sdk_test.go: TestSDKSettlementDeadline)
  • 2.7 CompleteBatch settles many messages in one transaction with the same per-item fencing + idempotency; a stale token without an exact-request receipt yields ok=false, never failing the batch. Single Complete and a CompleteBatch item share the completed operation identity, so the same successful request can replay in either direction. (engine/complete_batch_test.go: TestCompleteBatch, TestSettlementReceiptIdentityMatrix)
  • 2.8 RenewBatch extends a whole batch's leases in ONE statement, fenced per item on its own lock_token, and reports the deadline it committed. ok=true means the lease was live when the broker's STATEMENT finished — the answer still has to travel, so locked_until_ms is the authoritative fact and remote callers map it from broker time onto a local monotonic clock. A renewal whose write outlived the lock reports ok=false rather than handing back a lock the caller never held, and a renewal never shortens a lease. Each successful item uses the same deadline rule as §2.5 and preserves state, token, and delivery_count. Capped at 512 messages — a claim about a live lease is only keepable within a single statement. (engine/complete_batch_test.go)

3 · Idempotency & at-least-once

  • 3.1 Every Open MUST preserve an unexpired lease on an active resource and reclaim only locked_until <= now by default, because a new process cannot prove that no remote or out-of-process holder may still renew or settle its persisted token. An embedded owner MAY explicitly request immediate live-lease recovery only when all prior handlers are known to be gone. Resource lifecycle and message TTL remain authoritative. Reclamation follows the reaper rule: back to active, or to dead_lettered (MaxDeliveryCountExceeded) once delivery_count >= max_delivery_count. Preserving a live lease MUST NOT increment delivery_count. (engine/engine_test.go: TestExplicitCrashRecoveryRespectsMaxDelivery, TestOpenPreservesUnexpiredLeaseByDefault, TestOpenReclaimsExpiredLeasesByDefault)
  • 3.2 While its exact-request receipt is live, a settle whose response was lost MUST replay as success, not ErrLockLost — and ONLY when it is the same request. The receipt expires 30 minutes after recording; replay MUST NOT refresh that deadline. Resource deletion or fixed subscription expiry can end replay earlier. A settlement_receipt identifies queue + seq_number + lock_token + operation + effect-bearing arguments; a call that differs in ANY of them is not a replay and MUST return ErrLockLost, never a success that silently keeps the first call's effect. (engine/ga_fixes_test.go; engine/complete_batch_test.go: TestReceiptsAreBoundToTheirMessage, TestReceiptsAreBoundToTheirArguments, TestSettlementReceiptsAreVerbSpecific, TestSettlementReceiptIdentityMatrix; engine/model_test.go: TestEngineMatchesTheModel, TestModelRejectReceiptArguments)
  • 3.3 A Peek-Lock Receive retried with the same AttemptID MUST replay the same batch and tokens only while its record is live and every cached token still owns the corresponding live, unexpired lock. If any token is stale, the broker MUST invalidate the whole cached batch and safely perform a new claim in the same transaction; it MUST NOT return a stale or partially owned batch. This invalidation MUST NOT revoke any other token from that response that still owns a live lease; the caller that observed the original response may still be processing it. AttemptID is therefore only an exact retry key for a Receive whose response was not observed, and MUST NOT be reused for a new Receive after the response arrives or after partial settlement. A tokenless Receive-and-Delete response remains replayable for the attempt lifetime. For either mode, a record's lifetime is the greater of five minutes and the queue lock duration when recorded, capped by fixed subscription expiry. Replay and lease renewal MUST NOT extend the record's deadline. A live non-empty saved response is bound to its original receive mode; an empty result creates no record, and an expired record no longer binds the ID. Unknown modes MUST be rejected. Record and lease expiry MUST be checked against fresh time after writer admission. (engine/ga_fixes_test.go; engine/functional_test.go: TestReceiveAttemptExpiryAfterWriterWait, TestReceiveAttemptDoesNotReplayStaleLeaseAfterRestart, TestReceiveAttemptDoesNotReplayDeadLetteredLeaseAfterRestart, TestReceiveAndDeleteAttemptStillReplaysAfterRestart, TestReceiveAttemptDoesNotReplayExpiredLease, TestReceiveAttemptRejectsModeMismatchWithoutDestroyingReplay, TestReceiveRejectsUnknownModeWithoutMutation, TestEmptyReceiveAttemptDoesNotBindMode, TestExpiredReceiveAttemptDoesNotBindMode, TestReceiveAttemptInvalidatesWholePartiallySettledBatch)
  • 3.4 No message loss + no content corruption: the hermetic integrity workload sends a contiguous 1..N sequence with random bodies (hashed into a property), then consumes concurrently with intentional redelivery and a sufficient delivery budget. Every identity MUST be completed and each received body MUST match its hash. Repeated receives are expected; this is not an exactly-once handler guarantee. (engine/integrity_test.go TestMessageIntegrity)

4 · Deduplication

  • 4.1 Within a queue's dedup_window, a repeat message_id (empty → body SHA-256) with the same body MUST collapse to a single enqueue. Dedup is disabled when the configured window is zero (the default). Its window starts at the last new enqueue for the key; duplicates MUST NOT refresh it. Completion MUST NOT erase the retained dedup identity. Only body bytes participate in the conflict check; duplicate metadata, TTL and scheduled time MUST NOT update the original message. (engine/functional_test.go, engine/turso_test.go)
  • 4.2 A single Send whose message_id conflicts with a different body MUST return ErrDedupConflict (HTTP 409). (server/send_dedup_test.go)
  • 4.3 In a multi-message Send, a conflicting slot comes back as seq 0 (skipped) while the rest of the batch commits. (wire SendResponse; server/send_dedup_test.go)

5 · Ordering modes

  • 5.1 standard — per-GroupID FIFO with cross-group parallelism; messages with no GroupID are unordered. Claim eligibility is identical to group_fifo — the only difference is group_fifo additionally requires a GroupID at send time. (engine/functional_test.go)
  • 5.2 group_fifo — strict FIFO per GroupID (head-of-line per group); a send without a GroupID MUST be rejected with ErrGroupRequired. (engine/functional_test.go)
  • 5.3 strict_fifo — global FIFO: at most one message in flight for the queue at a time. (engine/functional_test.go, engine/claim_plan_test.go)
  • 5.4 Head-of-line MUST survive lock expiry: an expired-but-not-yet-reaped lock still blocks its group (strict_fifo: the whole queue) — successors are never delivered ahead of the expired head, and once the reaper resettles it the head is redelivered first, in id order (or dead-lettered at count ≥ max, which unblocks the group). The accepted cost is a group stall of up to one reaper interval on a consumer timeout. (engine/functional_test.go: TestFIFOHoldsAcrossLockExpiry)
  • 5.5 Head-of-line MUST survive an explicit backoff: Abandon with delay_ms > 0 parks the head in scheduled — a state the head-of-line probe covers — so successors are never delivered ahead of a backing-off head; when the backoff lapses the scheduler re-activates it and it is redelivered first. Other groups (other queues' worth of work under standard/group_fifo) proceed during the backoff. (engine/functional_test.go: TestAbandonDelayHoldsGroupOrder)

6 · Dead-letter queue

  • 6.1 Reaching max_delivery_count on an ordinary Peek-Lock Receive MUST NOT itself dead-letter the message: the Nth ordinary Peek-Lock claim is a full final attempt and may be renewed and completed. If that locked attempt is Abandoned, its lease expires, or it is recovered at startup with delivery_count >= max_delivery_count, it MUST be dead-lettered with reason MaxDeliveryCountExceeded instead of becoming active for an ordinary Peek-Lock N+1 claim. This ordinary retry bound does not override the explicit ReceiveDeferred behavior in §2.4. (engine/engine_test.go)
  • 6.2 Redrive moves dead letters back to active (or to a target queue); Purge permanently deletes them (scoped by Max/OlderThanMs). (engine/redrive — functional tests)

7 · Scheduling, deferral & TTL

  • 7.1 Schedule keeps a message hidden (scheduled, visible_at in the future) until its time, then the scheduler activates it; Cancel deletes a scheduled message that has never been delivered (delivery_count=0) — a backoff-parked redelivery (§2.2) is NOT cancellable and stays under the retry/DLQ discipline. Scheduler activation MUST NOT increment delivery_count. (engine/functional_test.go: TestAbandonDelayHoldsGroupOrder)
  • 7.2 TTL — an expired message (expires_at) MUST move to the DLQ when the queue has dead_letter_on_expire, else be discarded. The two branches cover the same state set — every non-terminal state including scheduled. The TTL sweep can expire a scheduled row directly. If the scheduler observes an overdue row first, it may change that row to active, but claim eligibility still excludes it at now >= expires_at; the TTL sweep then terminates it without delivery. The queue default is both the default and ceiling for an explicit message TTL. Expiry is anchored at the message's initial visible_at, so for scheduled messages the clock starts at their delivery time; later delayed Abandon and scheduler activation MUST NOT recompute it. Message TTL is independent of the lock lease: it may expire a locked row, and Renew MUST NOT extend it. Embedded and remote batch Send MUST preserve each item's requested TTL; a uniform HTTP batch may use the batch-wide field, while a mixed batch uses per-message fields. A request that combines a positive batch-wide TTL with positive per-message TTLs, or supplies a negative TTL in either location, MUST fail as invalid. The Go SDK MUST also reject a positive message TTL below the wire's 1 ms precision before sending or writing, and an effective deadline that overflows epoch milliseconds MUST fail without committing any item in the batch. (engine/functional_test.go: TestTTLScheduledToDeadLetter, TestTTLCapAtQueueDefault, TestNegativeMessageTTLRejectedBeforeWrite, TestMessageTTLExpiryOverflowRejectedAtomically, TestMessageTTLDeadlineSurvivesRenewAndDelayedRetry; sdk_test.go: TestBatchTTLRemoteEmbeddedParity, TestNegativeMessageTTLSDKParity, TestRemoteBatchTTLWireCompatibility; server/send_dedup_test.go: TestServerSendPerMessageTTL; engine/turso_test.go: TestTursoMessageTTLParity; test/api_tests.py: t_message_ttl_contract)

8 · DLQ retention

  • 8.1 With a bound set, reapDLQ MUST drop oldest-first dead letters past the max age, per-queue count, or per-queue body bytes — and MUST touch only state='dead_lettered' (never undelivered/in-flight/scheduled work). These are asynchronous retention targets rather than admission limits; a DLQ MAY exceed them temporarily between bounded worker passes. (engine/retention_dlq_test.go)
  • 8.2 With no bound (the engine default), the DLQ is unbounded — no auto-deletion. (engine/retention_dlq_test.go TestDLQRetentionDisabledByDefault)
  • 8.3 Each queue's effective bound is its own override resolved against the engine default (effectiveBound): 0 inherits the default, >0 overrides it, <0 is explicitly unbounded. (engine/retention_dlq_test.go TestEffectiveBound, TestDLQRetentionPerQueueOverride, TestDLQRetentionPerQueueInheritAndOptOut)

9 · Auth & errors (broker)

  • 9.1 When MQLITE_TOKENS is set, every endpoint MUST require a valid Authorization: Bearer token except the open / (discovery), /healthz, and the static admin console under /ui (when enabled — its own API calls still carry a token); a missing/invalid/expired/revoked token → 401 unauthenticated. (server/errors_test.go, server/index_test.go, server/console_test.go)
  • 9.2 Errors use a JSON envelope {code,message} with the documented HTTP status; not_found may add the backward-compatible resource discriminator queue or subscription: 400 invalid_argument/group_required · 401 unauthenticated · 403 permission_denied · 404 not_found · 409 already_exists/lock_lost/name_conflict/key_conflict/ queue_not_empty/subscription_not_empty · 413 message_too_large · 429 resource_exhausted · 499 canceled · 500 internal · 503 unavailable/outcome_unknown. (server/errors_test.go; see api-reference.md)
  • 9.3 Every registered RPC MUST bind a permission in the route registration. Send/Schedule/Cancel require send; all other QueueService methods require listen; subscription upserts and filter dry-runs require listen; all other AdminService and all AuthService methods require manage, except Observe and the opt-in /metrics endpoint also accept configured read-only monitor credentials. Both empty-only and forced subscription deletion require manage. Metrics MUST be disabled by default, return 404 while disabled, and appear as /metrics in discovery only while enabled. Enabling metrics MUST require administrator auth. Manage includes both data permissions. Configured and managed administrators MUST have identical operation rights, including issuing manage keys. Insufficient permission MUST fail before the handler can read or change protected data. (server/errors_test.go: TestAccessKeyCompletePermissionMatrix, TestListenSubscriptionProvisioningBoundary; server/metrics_test.go: TestMetricsDefaultOffAndAnonymousObserveDenied, TestMetricsEnabledRequiresAdministratorAuthentication, TestMetricsPermissionMatrix, TestMetricsDisabledSkipsDatabaseAuthentication)
  • Configured monitor credentials MUST NOT grant message access or administration, MUST be distinct from administrators, and MUST remain usable for fault telemetry without database-backed authentication. Failed collection MUST omit queue gauges and explicitly report unavailable data, preserving real in-memory counters. (server/metrics_test.go: TestMonitorConfigurationFailsClosed, TestObserveStorageFailureAvailability, TestObserveAuthOutcomesAndWholeRequestCoverage)
  • 9.4 Managed keys MUST survive restart and store only a SHA-256 digest of their token. New tokens MUST be mqk_ plus 64 lowercase hex characters from a secure random source. Existing configured tokens remain accepted exactly. Only the successful creation response returns a secret; list, errors and logs MUST NOT return tokens or digests. A duplicate public ID MUST NOT mint a second credential. Auth-off mode MUST refuse key management. (engine/storage_test.go: TestAccessKeyLifecycle, TestAccessKeyValidation; server/errors_test.go: TestAccessKeyManagementLifecycleAndSecrecy, TestAccessKeyErrorsDoNotEchoSecrets; token_test.go)
  • 9.5 Successful revocation MUST reject subsequent authentication; already authorized requests may finish. Static configuration takes precedence over a matching database record. The SDK MUST treat permission denial as permanent in receive, settlement and renewal paths, without unauthorized batch fallback. (server/errors_test.go: TestAccessKeyRevocationAndExpiryBoundaries; sdk_test.go: TestManagedKeySDKAuthorization; receiver_internal_test.go; cmd/mqlite/safety_test.go)
  • 9.6 Access-key lists MUST retain ID-ascending order by default. Explicit created_desc MUST order the complete result by creation time descending, then ID descending, with stable cursor pagination. Revocation MUST NOT move a key; insertion ahead of a cursor MUST NOT repeat or skip existing keys on later pages. Unknown sort values and unknown creation-order cursors MUST fail with invalid_argument. SDKs and tools MUST reject incorrectly ordered responses. (engine/storage_test.go: TestAccessKeyCreationOrderPagination, TestAccessKeySortValidationAndIndex; server/errors_test.go: TestAccessKeyCreationOrderHTTP; wire/wire_test.go: TestAccessKeyCreationOrderResponseValidation; test/api_tests.py)
  • 9.7 Every HTTP response MUST carry X-Mqlite-Server-Time-Ms, sampled from the same injectable epoch-millisecond broker clock used for lease and TTL decisions when the response is first written. The additive header is valid on both success and error responses; a client MUST NOT use a proxy-generated failure or redirect as evidence of broker time. A remote lease scheduler MUST apply transport and timestamp-precision uncertainty conservatively, reserve observed round-trip headroom for the next renewal, and MUST NOT extend a lease merely because its local wall clock falls inside that interval. A confirmed exact lease shorter than the managed Receiver's safe renewal interval MUST fail closed rather than enter an unbounded renewal loop. CORS-enabled responses MUST list the header in Access-Control-Expose-Headers. (server/errors_test.go: TestJSONResponsesCarryServerTime; receiver_internal_test.go: TestClientMapsBrokerDeadlineOntoLocalMonotonicClock, TestClientLongPollNeverExtendsLeaseFromLocalWallClock, TestClientLongPollObservationDoesNotContaminateShortRenewal, TestClientRejectsPathologicallyShortConfirmedLease)
  • 9.8 A managed Receiver that receives HTTP 499 while its own controlling context is still live MUST treat it as transient. A Receive replay MUST retain the same attempt ID. If the caller context is already canceled, it MUST stop without another request. (receiver_internal_test.go: TestReceiverRetriesBrokerCanceledReceiveWithSameAttemptID, TestReceiverDoesNotRetryBrokerCanceledResponseAfterCallerCancel)
  • 9.9 A managed Receiver MUST retain one non-empty AttemptID across every transient retry of one Receive round. Its first transient failure MUST add no client-generated delay unless a valid HTTP 429/503 Retry-After provides a positive pacing hint. Later failures use equal-jitter exponential backoff with a 500 ms base, doubling nominal windows and a three-second generated-delay cap. A valid hint MAY raise one wait above that cap but MUST be limited to 60 seconds; when it raises the generated delay, the error handler MUST be called before the wait, including on the first failure. Retry-After: 0 MUST NOT erase later generated backoff. Delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms are accepted. An absolute date uses the same response's parseable Date, otherwise the local response receipt time; malformed, negative, or overflowing values are ignored. Every wait MUST be interruptible by the controlling context. An HTTP status is transient under the 5xx rule only when status / 100 == 5; status 600 is not a 5xx and MUST be terminal. Any successful Receive, including an empty response, ends the round, resets its failure count, and gives the next round a fresh AttemptID. Renew and settlement retry policies MUST remain independent. (receiver_internal_test.go: TestReceiverRetryScheduleKeepsAttemptAndResetsAfterSuccess, TestReceiverRetryAfterIsBoundedManagedReceivePacing, TestParseRetryAfter, TestManagedReceiverHonorsHTTPRetryAfterAndKeepsAttemptID, TestReceiverCancellationInterruptsRetryAfterWait, TestReceiverReturnsNonRetryableHTTPError)

10 · Storage & schema invariants

  • 10.1 Local file / :memory: use a single writer (SetMaxOpenConns(1)); a second process / second OpenEmbedded on the same file MUST fail fast with ErrDBLocked. A local file MAY use one separate mode=ro plus query_only WAL connection for observation reads; it MUST reject writes and checkpoints and share the engine close gate. The global queue snapshot MAY be reused for about 10 seconds, MUST preserve its original sampled_at_ms and internal topology fence as one cache entry, MUST coalesce concurrent refreshes, and MUST NOT cache a failed refresh. Observe server_time_ms MUST be read separately from the same injectable lifecycle clock and MUST NOT be retained in that queue snapshot cache. Per-queue Stats remains a fresh indexed read. (engine/storage_test.go, engine/observability_performance_test.go)
  • 10.2 Open MUST refuse a DB whose recorded schemaVersion differs from the binary's (ErrSchemaVersionMismatch) rather than running mismatched DDL against it. (engine/storage_test.go)
  • 10.3 All times are epoch-ms (UTC); the clock is injectable for deterministic tests. The remote (Turso) path retries transient errors with backoff; the local path never retries. A successful null-baton libsql:// response closes that logical Hrana stream: it MUST NOT be retained in an idle slot or handed directly to a waiting caller. One transaction MUST remain on one logical stream through commit or rollback, and the local pool MUST remain MaxOpen=1 with no connection lifetime recycling. (engine/storage_test.go: TestHranaClosedStreamIsDiscardedBeforeFreshReuse, TestHranaTransactionKeepsOneLease, TestMemoryDBSurvivesRepeatedFreshStatements; engine/turso_test.go)
  • 10.4 Access-key table and index additions remain independently additive inside the canonical schema. Verify complete backup/restore content, including active, expired and revoked credentials. An incompatible existing object named access_keys or idx_access_keys_created MUST fail rather than be overwritten or silently trusted. (engine/storage_test.go: TestAccessKeySchemaAdditiveCompatibility, TestAccessKeySchemaConflict, TestAccessKeyCreationIndexUpgradeAndConflicts; test/production/restore/run.py, compat.py)
  • 10.5 Durable resource lifecycle and fixed subscription-expiry columns and indexes make the v0.4.0 schema token 7 incompatible with the older schema-5 layout and intermediate schema-6 layout. Each binary MUST refuse the other's database rather than adding columns, restamping the token or partially opening it. Operators must create a fresh database and preserve the matching old binary/backup pair. (engine/storage_test.go: TestSchemaVersionGuard, TestSchemaContentPinnedToVersionToken)
  • 10.6 Backend parity. Given the same committed state, broker time and request, local SQLite and remote Turso/libSQL MUST produce the same successful result, validation outcome, state transition and logical sentinel error. Latency, temporary availability, remote transport failures (including ErrOutcomeUnknown), remote transaction-callback replay and explicitly operational deployment, maintenance and observation behavior MAY differ; they MUST NOT silently change deterministic queue semantics. (engine/turso_test.go: TestTursoIntegration, TestTursoExtended, TestTursoMessageTTLParity, TestTursoConcurrent, TestTursoBatchSettle; engine/storage_test.go; server/errors_test.go; sdk_test.go)

11 · Subscription filters

  • 11.1 A subscription filter is one expr boolean predicate over the message; an empty filter matches every message. It is compiled + type-checked at Subscribe, and a malformed / unknown-field / non-boolean expression MUST be rejected with ErrInvalidFilter (HTTP 400 invalid_argument) and not stored — no backing queue is created. (engine/filter_test.go, server/errors_test.go)
  • 11.2 The filter is evaluated at publish against the message env (core fields, enqueued_at/visible_at, the derived subject_parts/body_size/property_keys, and the body fields body_text/body_json — projected only when referenced, with body_json decoded only for a JSON content type, else {}); a message is routed to a subscription if and only if its filter returns true. enqueued_at is the publish time and visible_at is the delivery time (equal for an immediate send, the scheduled time for a delayed one), so a delay is visible_at - enqueued_at. (engine/filter_test.go TestFilterFanoutConditions, TestFilterScheduledMessageDelay)
  • 11.3 Evaluation is fail-closed: a filter that errors or panics at runtime MUST leave the message unrouted to that subscription (logged) — never crashing the broker and never matching by default. (engine/filter_test.go TestEvalFilterFailClosed)
  • 11.4 Publishing to a topic that no subscription filter accepts is a valid no-op (SendOne/Schedule return 0, nil), not an ErrDedupConflict. (engine/filter_test.go TestFilterReSubscribeRecompiles)

12 · Topics & naming

  • 12.1 Plain-queue names, subscription names (their backing queues) and topic names are one disjoint namespace. Every collision MUST be rejected with ErrNameConflict (HTTP 409) at creation time, in both directions: Subscribe rejects a topic naming any existing queues row (plain or backing), a subscription name that is a plain queue / another topic's subscription / a live topic, and topic == name; CreateQueue rejects a name that is live as a topic and any cross-kind upsert. Same-kind upserts (queue reconfig, (topic,name) re-subscribe) stay open. A failed creation MUST leave nothing behind (guards + inserts are one transaction). (engine/functional_test.go: TestTopicQueueNamespaceDisjoint, TestTopicSubscriptionIsolation)
  • 12.2 Because names are disjoint, send/publish resolution is unambiguous: an active plain-queue or backing-queue name addresses that queue; an implicit topic name addresses its active subscription rows; any other name returns ErrQueueNotFound. Behavior after directly altering internal tables to create a queue/topic collision is outside the public contract. (engine/functional_test.go: TestTopicQueueNamespaceDisjoint)
  • 12.3 Subscription lifecycle. Deletion MUST select the exact (topic,name) pair. By default it MUST reject every retained message state with ErrSubscriptionNotEmpty; force is durable authorization to discard all states. Acceptance MUST atomically exclude the backing queue from fan-out and the data plane and start bounded cleanup. If that cleanup finishes in the accepting transaction, it MUST remove the queue and mapping and return deleted. Otherwise it MUST commit a deleting marker that preserves the mapping and name until a later transaction removes both. Restart MUST resume accepted pending cleanup without another force authorization. The last active subscription's retirement makes its implicit topic unavailable immediately.
  • 12.4 Bounded inventory. The compatibility ListSubscriptions operation MUST return every active subscription in (topic,name) order. The paged operation MUST use the same order, default to 100, reject limits above 1,000, return an exact total for the request's scope and optionally include deleting entries. Every paged row MUST carry required non-negative created_at_ms and expires_at_ms; zero expiry means permanent and a positive expiry MUST be greater than creation. An expired retained row is logically deleting. Its opaque cursor MUST be bound to the topic and include-deleting scope. One request is a consistent snapshot; pages issued as separate requests do not promise a frozen snapshot under concurrent changes.
  • 12.5 Capacity. The engine MUST bound active plus deleting subscriptions (default 10,000). Creating a new mapping at the bound returns ErrSubscriptionLimit (HTTP 429 resource_exhausted); re-subscribing an active exact pair may update its filter. A deleting entry MUST retain its slot until final physical cleanup. Public CreateQueue(kind=subscription) MUST NOT create a backing queue without a subscription mapping.
  • 12.6 Fixed subscription lifetime. A positive creation TTL MUST store one absolute deadline from the first successful transaction. Omitted/zero TTL on a new subscription makes it permanent; on an existing subscription it preserves the original lifetime. The same positive TTL is idempotent, while a different positive TTL MUST return ErrNameConflict before changing the filter. Retry, filter update, message activity and restart MUST NOT extend the deadline. At now >= expires_at fan-out and every direct data-plane effect MUST reject the subscription, cached metadata included. Locks and long polls MUST end no later than the deadline; Renew MUST NOT extend it, and idempotency records MUST NOT authorize work after it. (engine/functional_test.go, engine/engine_test.go, engine/complete_batch_test.go; sdk_test.go; server/subscriptions_test.go)
  • 12.7 Expiry cleanup. Expiry is durable advance authorization to discard all retained message states. The indexed scanner MUST transition due subscriptions to the existing restart-safe deletion lifecycle, while correctness remains independent of scan timing. Empty subscriptions MAY use set-based cleanup only when mapping and backing rows are removed in one transaction with exact row counts, including when foreign keys are off. Nonempty subscriptions remain subject to the global row/byte/fairness bounds, and every retained row keeps its capacity slot until physical removal. (engine/lifecycle_test.go, engine/storage_test.go)

13 · Cancellation (context deadlines)

Cancelling a call is not a way to undo it, and on a local store it is not a latency knob either. The rules below are the whole contract; they are stated here, and not only in the changelog, because a caller can observe every one of them.

  • 13.1 A mqlite operation whose context is already cancelled MUST NOT execute anything. This holds at both boundaries — before the wait for the writer, and again after the connection is in hand — and before entering a local Tx callback. (engine/cancel_test.go: TestPreCancelledNeverExecutes, TestCancelInTheHandoffWindowStartsNothing, TestNothingBeginsInTheLastWindowBeforeAStatement; sdk_test.go: TestEmbeddedTxCancellation)
  • 13.2 A caller waiting for the single writer keeps its own deadline: cancelling while queued MUST return promptly and MUST mutate nothing. (engine/cancel_test.go: TestCancelWhileWaitingWritesNothing)
  • 13.3 On a local store (file or :memory:), a statement that has already begun executing MUST be allowed to finish. It is not interrupted, and there is no upper bound on how long it takes — EngineTx.SQL() runs arbitrary user SQL, a full VACUUM rewrites the file, a large Purge is a big DELETE. A write can therefore commit after its caller has given up. This is deliberate: interrupting a local statement leaks the driver connection, which leaves a file DB locked (SQLITE_BUSY, permanently) or destroys a :memory: DB outright. (engine/cancel_test.go: TestCancelStormLeavesTheDatabaseUsable, TestCancelledSettleWritesLeaveTheDatabaseUsable)
  • 13.4 Inside a local transaction, mqlite-owned statements (including EngineTx.SendOne) check the caller's context before each statement: one already running finishes, and a statement whose check observes cancellation MUST NOT begin. EngineTx.SQL() exposes a raw *sql.Tx outside those guards for caller-owned tables; directly modifying mqlite-owned tables is outside the supported contract. Its statements MUST use tx.Context() to avoid interrupting local SQLite; that context is deliberately not cancellable, so raw SQL can still execute after the caller cancels. Callers MUST check the original context between their own statements and return promptly. Mqlite cannot interrupt the callback or release the single writer before it returns. Cancellation observed after the callback and before commit MUST roll back the whole transaction, including raw SQL writes, even if the callback returned nil. (engine/cancel_test.go: TestCancelledTransactionStopsIssuingStatements, TestTxCancelledBetweenStatementsRollsBack; sdk_test.go: TestEmbeddedTxCancellation)
  • 13.5 On a remote (Turso/libSQL) store, statement cancellation is real and unchanged: those statements can genuinely block on the network, and a discarded connection there holds no local lock.
  • 13.6 Follows from 13.3: a lost response never means "it did not happen". Cancellation does not change the at-least-once contract — reconcile, do not assume.

14 · Concurrency invariants

The properties a user cannot work around, asserted under real parallelism rather than by asking the engine to grade itself — an engine with a bug reports that everything is fine.

  • 14.1 Exclusive delivery. While a consumer holds a live lock on a message, that message MUST NOT be delivered to anyone else. Exclusivity is the lease: past locked_until the holder owns nothing, and a redelivery then is the at-least-once contract working, not a violation. (engine/concurrency_test.go: TestConcurrentConsumersNeverShareAMessage)
  • 14.2 The fence must fence. When a lock expires and the message is reassigned, a settle from the OLD holder MUST be refused (ErrLockLost) and the new holder's MUST succeed. "Exactly one winner" is not sufficient — the winner must be the holder of the live lock. (engine/concurrency_test.go: TestConcurrentSettlementPicksExactlyOneWinner)
  • 14.3 No zombie delivery. A completed message MUST NOT be delivered again. (engine/concurrency_test.go)
  • 14.4 No loss in the concurrency workload. With successful sends, live consumers, a sufficient delivery budget and no configured discard or expiry, every sent identity MUST be completed. This does not override final-attempt DLQ, explicit deletion, retention, message TTL or fixed subscription expiry. (engine/concurrency_test.go)
  • 14.5 Shutdown fences the store. Close closes admission before anything else: DB work that begins after shutdown starts MUST fail fast with ErrClosed; work already admitted — a statement, row scan, transaction callback, or commit in flight — MUST complete before the file lock is released, and a second Open on the same file during that window MUST be refused (ErrDBLocked); an empty long-poll Receive MUST be woken with ErrClosed rather than sleeping out its poll window against a closed engine. Close MUST NOT be called from inside a Tx callback — it waits for the callback, so that deadlocks. (sdk_test.go: TestEmbeddedCloseWaitsForPublicTx · engine/storage_test.go: TestCloseWaitsForInFlightWritesBeforeReleasingTheLock, TestCloseWakesLongPollWaiters)

15 · Crash recovery (process death)

Asserted by killing a real process hard (SIGKILL / TerminateProcess — no cleanup, no flush) while it is mid-transaction, restarting, and checking what survived. This covers process death, NOT power loss: a hard kill does not lose data the OS already accepted, so it exercises application-level recovery, not filesystem durability.

  • 15.1 Outbox atomicity across a crash. A transaction that writes a business row AND enqueues a message commits both or neither. After recovery the set of business rows equals the set of messages exactly: never an order without its message, never a message without its order. What each crash mode establishes, stated exactly:

    • Coordinated mode (deterministic): every run crashes the producer with a transaction held open between its two writes, so a torn callback — or an outbox split into two transactions — is caught on every run.
    • Random mode (activity deterministic, placement probabilistic): each kill is gated on stream-order evidence — two post-challenge ACKs, one discounted as a possible pre-challenge straggler — so every kill window provably contains a commit made after the liveness challenge, on any host: the evidence is a wait condition on the kill, not a throughput floor a slow runner could trip (per-window counts are logged). On a normally loaded host the evidence exists long before the kill timer expires, so the kill stays purely timer-driven. A frozen work loop never produces the evidence and fails deterministically. Where each kill lands within that live stream is probabilistic, so a crash falling exactly inside a hypothetical two-commit gap is supplementary coverage, not a per-run guarantee.

    (test/crash/crash_test.go: TestCrashOutboxAtomicity)

  • 15.2 Startup recovery respects lease ownership. Open preserves an unexpired lock on an active resource by default, including its token and delivery count, so a holder can continue across another process opening the store; a cached Peek-Lock attempt may replay that same valid token. Once the lease is expired, startup reclaims it to active, or to dead_lettered with MaxDeliveryCountExceeded if it was the last permitted delivery (the same rule the reaper applies, §3.1). A cached attempt MUST NOT replay a token invalidated by that recovery; its retry either obtains a currently valid new lease or observes no available message. Explicit embedded live-lease recovery follows the same transition immediately and is invalid in broker mode. (test/crash/crash_test.go: TestCrashRecoveryResetsOrphanedLocks, TestCrashRecoveryDeadLettersLastDelivery, TestCrashRecoveryInvalidatesReceiveAttemptLease; engine/functional_test.go: TestReceiveAttemptDoesNotReplayStaleLeaseAfterRestart, TestReceiveAttemptDoesNotReplayDeadLetteredLeaseAfterRestart; engine/engine_test.go: TestOpenPreservesUnexpiredLeaseByDefault, TestOpenReclaimsExpiredLeasesByDefault; shutdown_internal_test.go: TestReceiverSurvivesBrokerRestart)

  • 15.3 Acknowledged commits survive recovery. Every producer commit acknowledged to and observed by the harness before a kill MUST still be present after recovery. The harness checks those acknowledged transaction identities against both recovered business rows and messages. Commits whose acknowledgements were not observed remain subject to the all-or-nothing check in §15.1. (test/crash/crash_test.go: TestCrashOutboxAtomicity)

Run: make crash (race-instrumented, tag-gated; a separate Linux CI job, excluded from the default package matrix).

This spec is the contract a non-SQLite storage backend (see the Store-interface research) would have to satisfy to be a conformant mqlite. Hermetic package tests run with -race in the OS/Go matrix; tagged crash tests run with -race in their own Linux job. Live Turso tests run separately without -race; the large no-loss sweep also runs weekly without -race.
